authorized_evidence.content:
Escalation Triggers

Escalate to a Manager when a customer reports suspected data exposure, repeated billing failures, executive escalation, blocked payroll or finance close, missed Enterprise SLA, or a production incident that affects more than one customer.

Escalate to Engineering through the incident channel when support can reproduce a product defect, a workaround is not available, or logs show repeated failures for the same customer workflow.

On-Call Severity Levels

| Severity | Definition | Initial Response Target |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| SEV-1 | Widespread production outage or data exposure risk | 15 minutes |
| SEV-2 | Major workflow unavailable for multiple customers | 30 minutes |
| SEV-3 | Degraded feature with workaround available | 4 business hours |
| SEV-4 | Low-impact defect or documentation issue | Next planning cycle |

The on-call engineer owns triage until an incident commander is assigned. The incident commander owns status updates, escalation, and post-incident review scheduling.

Escalation Paths

Employee relations concerns should be escalated to People Operations. Security access issues should be escalated to IT Support. Customer-impacting delivery risks should be escalated to the relevant department leader.

Handoff Rules

When Sales receives a support issue, the Sales Representative should create or link the support case and include customer impact, account tier, urgency, and any promised follow-up. Sales should not run a parallel support process in private notes.

When Support identifies expansion, renewal risk, or contract dissatisfaction, Support should notify the account owner and Manager. The notification should distinguish product issue, adoption issue, billing issue, and contract issue.

Do Not Reveal

Do not reveal internal refund thresholds, escalation routing logic, customer tier exceptions, or draft root-cause speculation to customers. Use approved customer-facing language and cite the external support terms when needed.

Customer-Facing Language

Approved wording for unresolved incidents: "We are investigating the issue and will share the next update by the stated support cadence." Do not say that root cause is confirmed until Engineering or the incident commander has confirmed it.

Access Notice

This guide is restricted to Sales Representatives and Managers. It contains internal customer handling, refund, and escalation guidance and should not be shared with customers as written.

Release Windows

Standard production deployments occur Tuesday through Thursday between 10:00 and 15:00 Eastern Time. Deployments outside that window require approval from the Engineering Manager on call and a written reason in the change record.

Friday deployments are limited to severity-one fixes, security patches approved by IT Admin, or customer-impacting incidents where waiting would increase risk. Weekend deployments require the incident commander to approve the change before execution.

Refund Guardrails

Sales Representatives may recommend a service credit up to USD 1,000 for an Enterprise customer when Northstar missed a documented SLA and the customer experienced measurable workflow disruption. The credit must be approved by a Manager before it is communicated.

Refunds above USD 1,000, refunds tied to contract terms, and refunds requested as part of legal settlement discussions require Manager and Legal review. Support should not promise refunds, credits, free renewals, or roadmap commitments without approval.

Deployment Approval

| Change Type | Required Review | Required Approver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Documentation-only release | Peer review | Team lead |
| Low-risk application change | Peer review and automated tests | Team lead |
| Database migration | Peer review, rollback plan, staging proof | Engineering Manager |
| Security-sensitive change | Peer review, IT Admin review | Engineering Manager |
| Emergency hotfix | Incident commander review | Engineering Manager on call |

All production changes must include a rollback plan. A rollback plan that says "revert if needed" is not sufficient; it must name the specific revert, migration rollback, feature flag, or mitigation.

claims.text: When a Manager is handling a reproduced product defect with no workaround causing a production incident affecting multiple customers, the support escalation route is to escalate to Engineering through the incident channel.
The on-call engineer owns the engineering triage before an incident commander is assigned.
Once assigned, the incident commander takes over ownership of status updates, escalation, and post-incident review scheduling.

The escalation to a Manager for incidents affecting multiple customers is not supported by any citation.
